summary.headline: SKF India Q2 FY27 sales rose 16% YoY to about 2% QoQ growth, but EBITDA margin fell to about 14.5% as steel and supplier price increases ran ahead of customer price pass-through.
summary.overview: Management said sales grew 16% YoY and 2% QoQ, driven mainly by volume with marginal price or mix impact. EBITDA improved 155 bps YoY but fell 255 bps QoQ, as COGS rose from steel inflation and value-addition price increases given to suppliers. Customer price increases were agreed in some cases but not yet billed because purchase order amendments were pending, and management expects most recovery in the December quarter. Management also presented a new global brand identity and a hybrid-transmission EV bearing win from a major Indian OEM, with SOP around Q2 2028.

segments.name: OE (original equipment)
segments.commentary: Accounted for 66% of Q2 sales and 63% in H1. Two-wheelers were about 45-50% of OEM revenue, passenger vehicles 25-30%, and commercial vehicles 15-20%, per management's rough averages.

segments.name: Vehicle aftermarket (VA)
segments.commentary: Share of 19% in Q2 and 20% in H1. Volumes down about 7% YoY in Q2, similar to Q1, with management describing the decline as stabilised but margins still under pressure across hundreds of customers.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Share of 10% in Q2 and 9% in H1. Management guided to a range of around 10% of sales going forward, with quarterly variation from one-off transactions.

segments.name: SKF Industrial (post-demerger)
segments.commentary: Share of about 5% in Q2 and about 7% in H1. Trading with SKF Industrial is expected to fall to negligible levels over the next couple of years.

guidance_outlook: Price increases from customers are expected to be largely recovered in the December 2026 quarter, with a possible marginal spill-over into Q4 FY27.
Management expects EBITDA margin to return to the earlier guidance, which it said is above 15%, within FY27, not deferred to FY28.
Volume growth of 15% or slightly above is considered reasonable for FY28, with some new capacity replacing trading volumes and some revenue growth from price increases.
Total capex for the current year is expected to be close to INR 200 crore, part of a broader INR 500 crore-plus programme. The INR 140 crore announced is the SEBI-disclosed portion.
Export share expected to hold around 10% of sales.
capex_capacity: One new production line starts in the December 2026 quarter; another channel with capacity enhancement at Haridwar goes live around March 2027, and a third new channel comes from July 2027.
Traded goods imports are very small. Trading from SKF Industrial, which began after the demerger, is expected to decline to negligible levels over the next couple of years.
Ceramic bearings are made in India; the ceramic ball is a purchased component. The hybrid transmission programme starts production around Q2 2028.
Haridwar investment is capacity expansion for EV-specific bearings, mainly anchoring two-wheeler traction motor bearings; management said it will not monetise backward integration separately.
demand_pricing: Macro: GDP projected at 7.35% for the last quarter; CPI around 4.9%; manufacturing PMI 55.1 in September 2026; automotive production rose across all categories in the quarter.

Pricing: steel inflation and supplier value-addition price increases from April were absorbed in Q2. Customer price increases were partly agreed, with some effective January or July, but purchase order amendments were pending, so billing slipped.
Aftermarket competition: management said pricing pressure from hyper-competitive players has abated and margins are stabilising, but further action is needed.

Passenger vehicle programmes are tied to CAFE III norms. BS-7 discussions are at development stage with commercial vehicle customers, with high-efficiency product nominations expected around end-Q2 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall to about 14.5% and what drove other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall to steel and supplier value-addition cost increases from April, with customer price increases not yet billed. Other income includes forex gains, asset sales, rental and contract manufacturing income from SKF Industrial.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the customer price increase has been agreed, in negotiation, or refused?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give percentages. It said a large part should materialise in the December quarter, and some customers had earlier price increases effective January.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY28 growth assumption of 15-18% hold given capex schedules?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15% or slightly above is reasonable for FY28, citing new channels going live from December 2026 to July 2027, with some capacity replacing trading volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the content per vehicle for the EV hybrid transmission win?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ceramic bearing content is premium-priced and offsets fewer bearing positions in EV, so value per EV is marginally higher than ICE. Current volumes are modest.

qa_highlights.question: What is the right margin metric for investors, including or excluding other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin should be viewed excluding other income, but the company-level view should include it, since rental from SKF Industrial space would be redeployed to SKF India's own production.

qa_highlights.question: Are the other expense increases linked to demerger costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demerger-related expenses are over, and the rise reflects variable costs tied to about 20% volume growth, such as stores, power and fuel, and royalty.

risks_watch: Timing of customer price increase billing: the December quarter is the key test of whether the 255 bps QoQ margin hit reverses.
Steel and supplier cost inflation may persist if customer pass-through is only partial.
Aftermarket volumes are still down about 7% YoY, and margins are not yet recovering.
Other income (about INR 29 crore) includes non-recurring items such as forex gains and asset sales, so headline PBT may be flattered.
Demerger and SKF Industrial related-party dealings (trading, rental, shared services) will taper and could change the cost base.
Parent company listing in Stockholm on 1 December is a corporate-structure event to monitor.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth and the December-quarter margin recovery, but cautious and non-committal on price-increase quantum, customer percentages, and the exact timing of billing. The Q&A answers on other income and margin definitions were detailed but partly evasive.
